R.11-12.1: I can cite the most convincing evidence for complex inferences, explain where a text is ambiguous and pose questions that open new lines of inquiry.
I can cite strong text evidence for explicit and implicit meaning, identify where the text is ambiguous and develop questions for deeper understanding.
I can cite evidence for a stated inference and write one question about the text using sentence starters.
I can find a sentence that answers a direct question about the text with support.
I can analyze a text to determine its meaning and cite evidence to support what it says directly and indirectly.
R.11-12.2: I can write an objective summary that analyzes how two or more themes interact and build on each other to create a complex account.
I can objectively summarize a complex text and analyze how two or more themes or central ideas emerge and are shaped by specific details.
I can summarize a text and name one theme with supporting details using a graphic organizer.
I can retell the main events or ideas of a text using a word bank or pictures with help.
I can recount the main events or ideas of a text that relate to its theme or central idea.
R.11-12.3: I can evaluate how an author's choices about character, setting or sequence shape the whole text's meaning and effect.
I can analyze the impact of an author's choices in literary texts and explain how individuals, ideas or events interact and develop in informational texts.
I can explain one author choice, such as where a story begins, and its effect using a frame.
I can name a character or event and tell one thing that happens to it with help.
I can tell how characters, people, settings, ideas or events change over the course of a text.
R.11-12.4: I can analyze how an author develops and refines a key term over a text and how word choices create layered tone and mood.
I can determine figurative, connotative and technical meanings and analyze how word choice and the refining of key terms affect meaning, tone and mood.
I can explain the meaning of a key term in context and how it affects tone using a vocabulary chart.
I can match key words in a text to their meanings with pictures or a word bank with help.
I can tell how words or phrases, including multiple-meaning words and figurative language, affect meaning.
R.11-12.5: I can evaluate how an author's structural choices create meaning and judge their effect on clarity, persuasion and audience appeal.
I can analyze how structure creates meaning in literary texts and evaluate how structure affects clarity, persuasion and appeal in informational texts.
I can identify the structure of a text and explain one way it helps the reader using a graphic organizer.
I can tell what happens at the beginning and end of a text with help.
I can use a text's ending or structure to tell how it affects the meaning of the whole text.
R.11-12.6: I can analyze how authors use irony, satire or understatement to shape messages and how their identity and culture influence perspective.
I can analyze how authors use point of view, perspective and purpose to shape explicit and implicit messages and how background affects perspective.
I can identify the author's purpose and point of view and one technique used to show it with support.
I can tell what the author thinks about a topic with help.
I can determine an author's point of view and compare and contrast it with my own.
R.11-12.7: I can evaluate how different adaptations reinterpret a source text and synthesize multiple sources to solve a complex problem.
I can analyze and evaluate how adaptations in different formats interpret a source text and integrate sources to address a question or solve a problem.
I can compare two versions of a story or two sources on a topic using a chart.
I can point to the same event in a text and in a video with help.
I can compare two interpretations of a story, drama or poem and use information from different media to answer questions.
R.11-12.8: I can apply a chosen lens to judge an argument's validity and explain how specific fallacies or insufficient evidence weaken it.
I can delineate and evaluate an argument through a lens such as logical fallacy or legal reasoning, judging whether evidence is relevant and sufficient.
I can identify the claim and evidence in an argument and tell whether the evidence is enough using a checklist.
I can tell what the author wants me to believe and one reason with help.
I can tell whether the claims and reasoning make an author's argument stronger.
R.11-12.9: I can develop and justify sophisticated criteria to evaluate texts and synthesize connections across cultures, identities and eras.
I can choose and develop criteria to evaluate the quality of texts and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultures, identities, eras and my own experiences.
I can use a given set of criteria to judge a text and make one connection to another text or my life.
I can tell whether I liked a text and connect it to my life with help.
I can evaluate the quality of texts and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultures, identities, eras and my own experiences.
W.11-12.1: I can combine reflective, formal and creative writing in sophisticated ways for real audiences and justify my choices.
I can write reflective, formal and creative pieces for both high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
I can write a short piece for a given purpose using a model and sentence frames.
I can dictate or write a few words to share an idea with support.
I can, with support as needed, dictate or write to share my ideas for different purposes.
W.11-12.2.a: I can write a sophisticated argument or literary analysis that weighs claims and counterclaims fairly and anticipates my audience's concerns.
I can write arguments that introduce precise claims, distinguish counterclaims, and develop both fairly with evidence, organized to show clear relationships.
I can write a claim, a counterclaim and evidence for each using an argument organizer.
I can say or write my opinion and one reason with help.
I can, with support, write or dictate an argument with a clear claim and valid reasons organized logically.
W.11-12.2.b: I can write an informative text that synthesizes the most significant evidence and uses formatting and multimedia to make complex ideas clear.
I can write informative texts that organize complex ideas clearly and develop the topic with the most significant facts, definitions, details and quotations.
I can write an informative text with headings, facts and quotes using a planning frame.
I can share facts about a topic using words, pictures or dictation with help.
I can, with support, write or dictate an informative text with well-chosen facts and quotes and a conclusion.
W.11-12.2.c: I can write a narrative that uses pacing, reflection and multiple plot lines to develop a complex experience or theme.
I can write narratives that engage the reader with context and point of view, using dialogue, pacing, description, reflection and a logical event sequence.
I can write a narrative with dialogue and a clear sequence using a story map.
I can tell or draw what happened first, next and last with help.
I can, with support, write or dictate a narrative with dialogue, details and characterization that tells events in order.
W.11-12.3.a: I can build a unified text where each part extends the last and end with a conclusion that adds insight beyond the text.
I can organize complex ideas so each new element builds on the last to create a unified whole, and write a conclusion that follows from the text.
I can organize my ideas into an introduction, body and conclusion that connect using a planning frame.
I can put my ideas in order (first, then, last) with support.
I can, with support, create a text with an introduction, body and conclusion.
W.11-12.3.b: I can use varied transitions and sentence structures to create seamless cohesion across complex arguments.
I can use appropriate, varied transitions and syntax to link major sections, create cohesion and clarify relationships among complex ideas.
I can use transitions from a word bank to link my paragraphs.
I can use simple linking words such as and, then or because with help.
I can, with support, use transitions and time-order words to link my ideas.
W.11-12.3.c: I can use metaphor, analogy and precise subject vocabulary to explain complex topics clearly and memorably.
I can use culturally-sustaining language, domain-specific vocabulary and techniques such as metaphor, simile and analogy to manage a complex topic.
I can add subject words and one simile or metaphor using a word bank.
I can use simple describing words to tell about a picture or topic.
I can, with support, use words that give specific details.
W.11-12.4: I can produce polished writing whose development, organization and style are expertly matched to task, purpose and audience.
I can produce clear and coherent writing whose development, organization and style fit the task, purpose and audience.
I can produce clear writing for a task using a model and checklist.
I can write or dictate a few sentences on a topic with help.
I can produce clear writing that fits a particular task, purpose and audience.
W.11-12.5: I can revise independently and strategically, focusing on what matters most for my purpose, and explain my revision choices.
I can plan, revise, edit, rewrite or try new approaches, alone and with others, focusing on what matters most for my purpose and audience.
I can revise my writing using feedback and a checklist with support.
I can make one change to my writing when an adult points it out.
I can, with support as needed, plan, write for a purpose, and revise and edit my writing.
W.11-12.6.a: I can evaluate and choose technologies that best connect my writing with real readers and explain why.
I can make informed decisions about technology use, assessing how well a tool connects writers and readers.
I can choose a tool to share my writing with readers from given options.
I can use a device to share a few words with help.
I can make intentional decisions about technology to produce, publish and update my writing.
W.11-12.6.b: I can design accessible digital writing experiences for specific audiences and justify my design choices.
I can make informed decisions about technology use, assessing how well a tool produces accessible experiences for specific audiences.
I can add one accessibility feature, such as captions or alt text, with support.
I can choose a picture or sound to go with my writing with help.
I can make intentional decisions about technology to produce, publish and update my writing.
W.11-12.6.c: I can flexibly combine modes such as text, image and sound to match my ideas and audience.
I can make informed decisions about technology use, assessing how well a tool matches modes with ideas to communicate with readers.
I can choose whether to use text, images or audio for my message with support.
I can add a picture to my writing with help.
I can make intentional decisions about technology to produce, publish and update my writing.
W.11-12.7: I can design and carry out sustained, authentic research, adjusting my inquiry and synthesizing many sources into new understanding.
I can conduct short and sustained research to answer a question or solve a problem, narrowing or broadening the inquiry and synthesizing multiple sources.
I can research a given question using several sources and a note-taking organizer.
I can find one fact about a topic in a source with help.
I can, with support as needed, conduct inquiry projects using information from several sources to answer a question or solve a problem.
W.11-12.8: I can use advanced searches, weigh each source's strengths and limits, and integrate evidence smoothly with correct citations.
I can gather information from authoritative sources with advanced searches, assess strengths and limitations, integrate it selectively and cite in a standard format.
I can find credible sources, paraphrase information and cite it using a template.
I can copy a fact and its source title with help.
I can write answers to research questions by selecting relevant information from several sources.
W.11-12.9: I can select and explain the most compelling evidence from complex texts to support sophisticated analysis and research.
I can draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection and research.
I can find a quote that supports my answer using a sentence starter.
I can point to a sentence that matches my idea with help.
I can, with support, use evidence from a text to support reflection, analysis or inquiry questions.
SL.11-12.1.a: I can come prepared with research and text evidence and use it to deepen and challenge the group's analysis.
I can come to discussions prepared with evidence from texts and research and use it to support analysis.
I can bring notes with evidence and share one point using a sentence frame.
I can share a fact or picture I prepared with support.
I can prepare evidence for discussions by collecting information and explain it.
SL.11-12.1.b: I can lead peers in civil, democratic discussions, set clear goals and reflect on group and personal progress.
I can work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and reflect on progress.
I can follow group goals and say one thing that went well using a reflection frame.
I can take turns and listen with adult support.
I can work with peers to set norms and goals for discussions and reflect on the conversation.
SL.11-12.1.c: I can ask probing questions that test reasoning and evidence and make sure every position gets a fair hearing.
I can propel conversations with questions that probe reasoning and evidence, ensure all positions are heard, and clarify or challenge ideas.
I can ask a question that asks for evidence using question stems.
I can answer a question about the topic with a word or picture with help.
I can ask and answer questions to check or clarify my ideas in a discussion.
SL.11-12.1.d: I can synthesize claims from all sides, resolve contradictions and identify exactly what research is needed next.
I can engage with diverse perspectives, synthesize claims and evidence from all sides, resolve contradictions and determine what more information is needed.
I can summarize two different views from the discussion using a frame.
I can show agree or disagree with a card or gesture with help.
I can respond appropriately to agreement and disagreement in a discussion.
SL.11-12.2: I can synthesize many media sources, resolve conflicting data and justify a decision based on the most credible evidence.
I can analyze and synthesize information from diverse media to make decisions and solve problems, evaluating credibility and noting discrepancies in data.
I can compare information from two sources and tell which is more credible using a checklist.
I can tell where a piece of information came from with help.
I can determine the credibility and accuracy of information from different media or formats.
SL.11-12.3: I can evaluate how a speaker's premises, rhetoric and tone work together and judge how convincing the argument is.
I can evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, evidence and rhetoric, assessing stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, emphasis and tone.
I can identify a speaker's claim, one piece of evidence and the tone using an organizer.
I can tell whether a speaker sounds happy, angry or serious with help.
I can tell whether a speaker's claims and reasoning make the argument stronger.
SL.11-12.4: I can deliver a compelling presentation that addresses opposing views and adapts substance and style to any audience.
I can present findings and evidence with a clear perspective and organization, address opposing views and use style that fits purpose, audience and situation.
I can present an organized argument with evidence using notes and a model.
I can share my opinion on a topic with a picture or sentence frame with help.
I can present an argument organized to fit the purpose, audience and task.
SL.11-12.5: I can design strategic digital media that deepens understanding of my reasoning and evidence and engages my audience.
I can make strategic use of digital media in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning and evidence and add interest.
I can add a chart, image or video clip that supports one point using given options.
I can choose a picture for my presentation with help.
I can use digital media strategically in presentations to support understanding and add interest.
L.11-12.1.a: I can analyze how the history of standardized English connects to power and argue for valuing linguistic diversity.
I can recognize that standardized English is one dialect of many and that its history is connected to power.
I can name differences between dialects I know with support.
I can notice that people speak in different ways in different places with help.
I can notice that standardized English is one dialect of many with a history connected to power.
L.11-12.1.b: I can analyze any situation's language demands and adapt my language precisely to author intent, genre and audience.
I can develop communicative competence by determining and responding to the language demands of varied situations, considering intent, context, purpose, genre and audience.
I can tell if a situation is formal or informal and adjust my words using a chart.
I can sort phrases into school talk and friend talk with help.
I can notice whether a situation is formal or informal and respond in an appropriate way.
L.11-12.1.c: I can critically evaluate my language and genre choices and revise them to be more effective for my purpose.
I can develop metacognitive awareness by justifying and evaluating how effective and appropriate my language and genre choices are.
I can explain why I chose a word or genre using a sentence frame.
I can point to a word I chose and say why with help.
I can explain the reasons for my language choices.
L.11-12.1.d: I can apply MLA, APA or other style manuals accurately and explain why disciplines use different conventions.
I can recognize that disciplines have style manuals, such as MLA and APA, and write and edit work to meet those expectations.
I can format a citation or heading in MLA using a template.
I can copy a source title in the right place with help.
L.11-12.1.e: I can analyze how complex syntax creates meaning in texts and vary my own syntax for deliberate rhetorical effect.
I can apply an understanding of syntax when reading complex texts and vary syntax for effect when writing.
I can break a long sentence into parts to understand it and combine two sentences in my writing with support.
I can say a complete simple sentence with an adult model.
I can use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating.
L.11-12.2.a: I can use print and digital references to analyze a word's etymology and usage and explain nuances in meaning.
I can determine a word's pronunciation, precise meaning, part of speech, etymology and usage and verify it with reference materials.
I can look up a word to find its meaning and part of speech with support.
I can find a word in a picture or online dictionary with help.
I can use context to determine the meaning of unknown words.
L.11-12.2.b: I can predict and explain how word changes shift meaning and part of speech across academic vocabulary.
I can determine and correctly use patterns of word changes that show different meanings or parts of speech, such as analyze, analysis and analytical.
I can complete a word family chart (analyze, analysis) using examples.
I can match a word to a picture of its meaning with help.
I can identify root words and the words formed by adding or removing affixes, and use references to clarify meanings.
L.11-12.3.a: I can analyze subtle differences between words with similar meanings and explain how they shape tone and argument.
I can determine denotative, connotative and figurative meanings of words and analyze nuances in words with similar denotations.
I can tell the difference in feeling between two similar words using a word scale.
I can tell whether a phrase means exactly what it says with help.
I can interpret common figures of speech.
L.11-12.3.b: I can analyze how word choices build cumulative effects and how texts blend linguistic diversity to engage readers.
I can analyze the cumulative impact of word choices on meaning, tone and effectiveness, including multiple meanings, engaging language and linguistic diversity.
I can find words that create a tone and explain their effect using a chart.
I can match a word to a happy or sad feeling with help.
I can determine the intended meaning of multiple-meaning words.
L.11-12.4: I can independently build vocabulary in several disciplines and choose words precisely for each context.
I can build vocabulary with others and on my own, including cultural, academic and subject terms, and choose words that fit the situation.
I can use new academic words from a word wall in my speaking and writing with support.
I can use a few key subject words with pictures and help.
I can use general academic and subject-specific words across contexts.
L.11-12.5.a: I can explain how conventions in different genres developed through agreed usage and apply them flexibly.
I can recognize that conventions of punctuation, layout and formatting in a genre are the result of agreed-upon usage.
I can name one convention of a genre, such as a letter or report, using examples.
I can point to a title or heading in a text with help.
I can use conventions of standard English when needed.
L.11-12.5.b: I can analyze how and why usage varies across communities and evaluate arguments about contested usage.
I can identify ways that usage and conventions vary and are sometimes contested.
I can name one example of a word or phrase used differently in two places with support.
I can notice that people say things in different ways with help.
L.11-12.5.c: I can resolve complex usage questions by comparing several references and explaining my decision.
I can resolve issues of complex or contested usage by consulting appropriate references.
I can look up a usage question in a given reference with support.
I can ask an adult to help check a word with help.
I can use digital, electronic and other tools to improve my use of language.
L.11-12.6.a: I can use sophisticated punctuation such as brackets, italics and expressive capitalization to create precise effects.
I can use sophisticated punctuation and capitalization techniques that fit the situation and genre.
I can use brackets or italics correctly in a research sentence using a model.
I can find capital letters and end marks in a sentence with help.
I can use capitals, end punctuation and spelling conventions when writing.
L.11-12.6.b: I can spell complex and discipline-specific words correctly and use resources to check unusual spellings.
I can spell correctly in my writing.
I can spell common words correctly and use a spell-checker for others.
I can spell my name and a few familiar words with help.
I can spell most single-syllable words correctly and use word chunks to spell longer words.
